---
title: "Teach and Share the Load"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** The Reviewer's Code. **Objective:** pass on what you learned without leaving anyone behind, and keep your own skills and workload healthy.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim. Team norms you agree locally override these defaults.</span>
:::

## Teaching

You do not need to be an expert to help. When teaching a colleague:

- **Start from their problem**, not from the tool.
- **Teach the checks first.** Verification habits matter more than clever prompts.
- **Let them predict, then reveal.** Ask "what do you expect this to do?" before running it.
- **Welcome opt-outs.** A colleague may choose not to use LLMs, and may still be an excellent reviewer.

## Protecting your own learning

An agent can quietly take over the parts you wanted to learn. Pick a rule that suits you, such as: write the first version of anything new yourself, then compare; ask the agent to **explain** rather than **do**; and keep one area of your work agent-free.

## Managing workload

Agents make it easy to start many things. Count the cost of **reviewing** what they produce. A simple rule: start no more than you can review today.

<div data-ao-honour="teach-one" data-xp="25">Show one colleague one verification habit from this odyssey, such as re-running the check, or running `awk` against a script's output. Teach the habit, not the tool.</div>

## Battle: the community
